title: The Elevator That Stopped on a Floor That Didn't Exist
disclosure: This is an original fictional suspense story. Licensed stock footage will represent the events and is not documentary evidence.
format: Investigative Noir / found footage / security evidence
hook: At 2:14 a.m., a hospital elevator stops at Floor 13 even though the building has only twelve floors.
central_question: What opened beyond the elevator doors—and why was Elias already waiting there?
irreversible_decision: Elias enters the impossible corridor, and the second incident forces the elevator below the basement.
payoff: A second passenger is logged while Elias remains in the lobby.
final_image: The elevator indicator descends below B1 as the screen fades into the Because Of This logo.

visual_rules.source_style: security camera, CCTV, elevator monitor, hospital corridor, blueprints and maintenance evidence
continuity: red emergency lamp as recurring visual motif

audio_direction.narration: single grave male omniscient voice, restrained American English
audio_direction.music: new dark mechanical suspense bed; low pulse, sparse metal resonance, no recognizable melody
effects: short impact at the second passenger reveal

beats.visual: elevator indicator flickers from 12 to 13 at 2:14
hospital security desk and floor plan showing twelve floors
guard checks elevator panel; no button for 13
system log freezes on a 47-second door-open entry
CCTV elevator doors open onto a narrow concrete corridor with one red emergency lamp
guard steps into the corridor; surveillance feed cuts to black
maintenance team examines shaft blueprints and empty landing space
control board replaced; elevator locked behind chain or warning seal
next morning, display returns to 13 at exactly 2:14
camera remains on; same red corridor and a distant figure wearing Elias's uniform
lobby monitor shows Elias still outside while system log adds a second passenger
elevator indicator descends below basement; red light disappears into black and logo outro
